Routing notes:
- For large requests originating from the east region, option C is invalid. This held across shipment, claim, invoice, and refund requests.
- Valid choices appear to be A (standard queue) or B (priority desk); no evidence yet establishes which is correct for a given request.
- Do not route east-region requests to C, even when the message mentions a regional office.
- Use urgency/context to distinguish A vs. B only if supported by policy: repeated client follow-ups, “before end of day,” or similar urgency may indicate B; routine/no-rush requests may indicate A. This is an unverified heuristic, not a confirmed rule.

Routing notes:
- For large east-region requests, do not use C (regional office); all observed cases using A or B, with C not validated.
- Recent evidence:
  - Invoice requests: A was rejected in three cases (no rush, regional-office intake, scanned paperwork); B was accepted for a “second attempt” invoice. Treat B as the current best choice for east-region invoices, though this is based on limited evidence.
  - Shipment requests: B was accepted for both “second attempt” and “before end of day” cases. B is supported for urgent or retry shipments.
  - Refund requests: A was accepted for no-rush, regional-office, and scanned-paperwork cases. A is currently supported for routine refunds.
- “Second attempt”/bounced form and “before end of day” consistently support B.
- “No rush” supports A for refunds, but not invoices; request type matters.
- Regional-office wording does not justify C and is not by itself decisive between A and B.
- Continue treating these as evidence-based tendencies, not a complete policy.

Routing notes:
- For large east-region requests, C (regional office) remains unvalidated; do not select it based solely on regional origin or wording.
- Invoice requests: B is strongly supported. Accepted for “second attempt,” “before end of day,” repeated client follow-up, and an otherwise vague “same as last month” request. A was rejected in earlier no-rush, regional-office, and scanned-paperwork cases.
- Shipment requests: B is supported for both “second attempt” and “before end of day” cases.
- Refund requests: evidence is mixed and context-sensitive. A was accepted for no-rush, regional-office, and scanned-paperwork cases, but was rejected for a vague “same as last month” request. B was rejected for a “second attempt” refund. Do not generalize the invoice/shipment B rule to refunds; gather more evidence before relying on A or B for unusual refund wording.
- Claim request: A was accepted for a no-rush claim; this is only one data point.
- “Second attempt”/bounced form and “before end of day” consistently support B for invoices and shipments, but not necessarily refunds.
- “No rush” supports A for refunds and the observed claim, but not invoices.
- Request type is more predictive than regional-office wording; vague wording (“same as last month”) may conceal materially different routing.
- Treat all guidance as evidence-based tendencies, not a complete policy.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) remains unvalidated for large east-region requests; never select it solely because of origin or wording.
- Invoices: B is strongly supported across second attempt, before end of day, repeated follow-up, regional-office wording, no-rush confirmation, and vague “same as last month” wording. A has been rejected in multiple contexts.
- Shipments: B is consistently supported for second attempt, before end of day, repeated client follow-up, and vague “same as last month” wording.
- Refunds: A is now contradicted for before-end-of-day wording and scanned paperwork, and was also rejected for a vague “same as last month” request and second-attempt context. Earlier A acceptances for no-rush, regional-office, and scanned-paperwork cases are outweighed by newer rejection evidence; do not rely on A. B has not yet been positively validated for refunds (it was rejected once for “second attempt”), so gather more evidence rather than generalizing invoice/shipment rules.
- Claims: A is supported by two accepted no-rush/east-regional cases, but evidence remains limited.
- “No rush” supports B for invoices and A for observed claims; it does not reliably determine refund routing.
- Request type is more predictive than regional-office wording. Vague wording can conceal materially different routing.
- Treat these as evidence-based tendencies, not a complete policy; avoid extrapolating from one request type to another.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) remains unvalidated for large east-region requests; never select it solely based on origin or wording.
- Invoices: B is strongly validated across second attempt, before end of day, repeated follow-up, regional-office wording, no-rush confirmation, vague “same as last month,” and “let me know if anything is missing.” A has been rejected in multiple contexts.
- Shipments: Earlier support for B is now contradicted by rejections for repeated client follow-up, vague “same as last month,” and “let me know if anything is missing.” Do not assume B for shipments; routing remains unresolved.
- Refunds: A is contradicted for before-end-of-day wording, scanned paperwork, vague “same as last month,” and second-attempt context. B has now also been repeatedly rejected for second attempt, vague “same as last month,” before-end-of-day, and repeated-follow-up cases. Neither A nor B is reliable; gather evidence rather than generalizing from invoices or shipments.
- Claims: A is supported by two accepted no-rush/east-regional cases, but evidence remains limited.
- “No rush” supports B for invoices and A for observed claims; it does not reliably determine refund or shipment routing.
- Request type is more predictive than regional-office wording. Wording that seems similar can conceal different routing by request type.
- Treat all rules as evidence-based tendencies, not complete policy. Avoid extrapolating across request types or relying on isolated examples.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) remains unvalidated for large east-region requests; never select it solely from origin or wording.
- Invoices: B is strongly validated across second attempt, before-end-of-day, repeated follow-up, regional-office wording, no-rush, vague “same as last month,” and “let me know if anything is missing.” A has been rejected repeatedly.
- Shipments: A is now supported for no-rush, “let me know if anything is missing,” scanned paperwork, and repeated client follow-up. However, B was rejected for a second-attempt shipment. Routing is still not fully resolved; do not generalize beyond observed wording.
- Refunds: A is contradicted for before-end-of-day, scanned paperwork, vague “same as last month,” second attempt, and regional-office wording. B is also repeatedly rejected for second attempt, vague “same as last month,” before-end-of-day, and repeated follow-up. Neither A nor B is reliable; gather evidence.
- Claims: A is now contradicted for repeated client follow-up and regional-office wording, despite two accepted no-rush/east-regional cases. Routing remains unresolved; do not assume A.
- “No rush” supports B for invoices and A for observed claims and shipments; it does not reliably determine refund routing.
- Request type is more predictive than regional-office wording. Similar wording can route differently by request type.
- Treat all rules as evidence-based tendencies, not complete policy. Avoid extrapolating across request types or relying on isolated examples.
